Assert that columns are constant within each unit

Source: R/ensure_constant.R
ensure_constant.Rd

A checkpoint for attributes that belong to the unit, not to the row: sex and birth date per person, the founding year per company. In a panel or a set of spells they are repeated on every row, and a unit with two values is an error, usually of linkage or of a register correction applied to some years only. On failure, every row of the units that vary is reported, so the conflicting values sit together. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_constant(
  data,
  id,
  ...,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

...

Columns that must be constant within a unit (tidy-select), e.g. sex, birth_date.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when a column varies and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

The same check covers hierarchies: that each settlement lies in one municipality, or each 4-digit code in one 2-digit code, is the parent column constant within the child, ensure_constant(places, settlement, municipality). With years, give both, ensure_constant(places, c(settlement, year), municipality), so a settlement may move between municipalities in a reform but not within a year.

A missing value does not break the rule: a sex that is missing in one year and known in another is incomplete, not contradictory. Find such units with describe_varying(), which counts them as partly missing.

See also

describe_varying() to see which columns vary, and how much.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(
  cpr  = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c"),
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2020, 2021, 2020, 2021),
  sex  = c("F", "F", "M", "F", "M", NA)
)
# b changes sex; c is only missing in 2021
ensure_constant(persons, cpr, sex)
#> Warning: Varies within units: sex per cpr
#> ℹ 2 rows
#>   In 1 unit
#> ℹ The rows:
#>     cpr   sex    year
#>     <chr> <chr> <dbl>
#>   1 b     M      2020
#>   2 b     F      2021
#> ℹ Which value holds is a choice, e.g. dplyr::mutate(persons, sex = <first, last or most common>, .by = cpr)
